previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, atrial fibrillation, esophageal stricture, and alcohol abuse was admitted after a fall at home associated with vomiting, tachycardia, and hypoxia. He was found to have aspiration pneumonia, likely due to his known swallowing dysfunction and esophageal abnormalities. Atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response resolved spontaneously but required rate control with increased diltiazem. He underwent esophageal dilation for a symptomatic stricture and was transitioned from IV to oral antibiotics. His hypothyroidism was addressed with an increased levothyroxine dose, and iron supplementation was started for anemia. He improved clinically, was weaned off oxygen, and tolerated a regular diet. He was discharged home with services on a full course of antibiotics, adjusted medications, and follow-up plans for thyroid testing and colonoscopy.
